simplicity-r1-f1.rationale: Partial — defending R6's configurable cap, accepting R11's flag drop. R6's `config.json.develop.greenBatchCap` is interview-grounded: interview Round 2 (line 78 of `002-develop-skill-interview.md`) records the user explicitly editing the AI's recommended default of 5 down to 3, with the rationale 'PR review fatigue kicks in faster than people expect, and a 3-task batch is the size where a reviewer can still catch a pattern-level concern.' The user's explicit edit is the documented consumer ask the Simplicity sub-clause requires; configurability lets projects with strong CI signal raise it (the user named this exact use case in Round 2). This is not speculative configurability — the configurable knob landed because the user surfaced two specific use cases (low-CI projects wanting smaller batches, high-CI projects wanting larger ones) during grilling. R11's `config.json.develop.codexAtGate4` is a different story: that knob was AI-recommended in Round 4 without a user-surfaced second consumer; the user confirmed Round 4 but did not edit-in additional use cases. The Simplicity concern is correct on R11 — that knob is speculative. Splitting the response: push back on R6, accept on R11.
simplicity-r1-f1.revision_applied: R6 retained as-is (configurable cap with default 3) — user's Round 2 edit is the documented consumer ask. R11 revised to drop `config.json.develop.codexAtGate4` and hard-code the v1 behaviour: 'Codex is invoked at Gate 5 only, not at Gate 4. v1 ships with this hard-coded; consumers who want Gate-4 Codex review can request it as a v2 enhancement when the use case surfaces.' AC-7 updated to drop the conditional second clause about `codexAtGate4`.

surgical-r1-f1.rationale: Cross-skill creep is real. AC-10 implicitly requires `specflow:misc --auto` payload schema fields that the current Phase 1 schema doesn't name. Option (b) (explicit dependency call-out) is the smaller change and preserves the Phase-2 PRD's scope; option (a) (reuse existing schema) constrains the misc-task entry's information value too much. Going with option (b).
surgical-r1-f1.revision_applied: AC-10 sharpened to add the explicit dependency: 'AC-10 depends on `specflow:misc --auto` accepting `manifest_path` and `gate_finding_id` as named fields. If the current Phase 1 schema does not include these, ship them via a separate `specflow:misc` enhancement PRD before `specflow:develop` v1 lands.' This makes the cross-skill dependency loud, not buried in implementation.

tbc-r1-f1.rationale: The unstated assumption is real and load-bearing. Without an explicit lane-recheck mechanism, R5 + AC-8 are non-firing in practice — none of the standard five reviewers have lane-checking as a documented lens. Option (a) (mechanical pre-Gate-4 lane-recheck) is more reliable than option (b) (extending Goal-Driven Reviewer's lens) because the recheck is a structured comparison (plan's actual file count vs scope's claimed file count, plan's modules vs scope's modules) that doesn't require reviewer judgement. Going with option (a).
tbc-r1-f1.revision_applied: Add a new requirement R0 (inserted before R1, since it's a pre-Gate-4 step in the skill flow) — actually R-numbering convention puts it as R5.5 conceptually; reordering to keep R-numbering sequential. Inserting as R5.5? No — renumbering is messy. Cleaner: keep R5 + AC-8 but add an explicit pre-Gate-4 mechanical recheck as a new requirement R5a (or treat as R6 and renumber subsequent). For surgical-edit reasons, splitting R5 into R5 (the trigger contract) and adding R5.1 as the mechanical recheck. Implementation: edit R5 to clarify that it's the post-mechanical-recheck reviewer-driven path, and add a new requirement after R5 specifying the mechanical pre-Gate-4 recheck step. Update AC-8 to verify both: the mechanical recheck fired AND any reviewer-driven re-lane was recorded.

tbc-r1-f2.rationale: R12's rationale phrasing was imprecise. DA cannot cover cross-provider concerns in same-provider review by definition. The manifest note is already the truthful framing; the rationale paragraph just needed to stop over-claiming.
tbc-r1-f2.revision_applied: R12's rationale rewritten to remove the 'DA covers cross-provider concerns' phrasing. New text: 'When Codex is absent, the standard five-reviewer set runs Gate 5 with Goal-Driven Reviewer load-bearing (code-vs-plan acceptance is its lens). Devil's Advocate runs as part of the standard set, but cross-provider review is not available — the manifest note is the authoritative framing of degraded coverage.' Manifest-note text retained verbatim.

goal-r1-f1.rationale: Orphan-AC gap is real. AC-13 enforces a PRD-anchor format that no R-level requirement establishes. The architectural rule (Phase 2 § scope item 7) is locked-in but needs R-level expression in this PRD body so downstream skills (`specflow:test`) can build a plan against the requirement. Adding R17 closes the gap.
goal-r1-f1.revision_applied: Added new requirement R17: 'Per-task plan's PRD-anchor format. Every per-task plan's first paragraph follows the format `"We're doing X because of PRD requirement Y. This aligns with Z."` where X paraphrases the task scope, Y is a literal `R{N}` from the feature's PRD, and Z paraphrases the requirement's `Serves goal:` field. Plans whose first paragraph doesn't match this format are a failed plan emission; Gate 4 must not be invoked until the format is satisfied. Trace: codebase context (pre-grilling) — Phase 2 § scope item 7 architectural rule. Serves goal: Outcome (PRD-anchored plan commentary).' AC-13's `Verifies:` line updated from 'R10's PRD anchor cross-check' to 'R17'.

goal-r1-f2.rationale: Goal-coverage gap is real. Goal Outcome surface (h) names task-history.json development-time field extension; no AC verifies it. Adding AC-15 closes the gap. Whether to also add an R-level requirement: the architectural Phase 3 scope item 1 already establishes the schema; R16 (orchestrator pattern) covers the file-write discipline; the AC alone suffices to bind the skill to the goal field.
goal-r1-f2.revision_applied: Added new acceptance criterion AC-15: 'On task completion (Verifier passes OR option 4 accept-and-ship is chosen per AC-12), the skill appends to (or updates) the matching `admin/task-history.json` entry with the development-time fields per `docs/PRD.md` Phase 3 scope item 1: `lane_assigned`, `ai_assistance_level`, `elapsed_minutes`, `what_worked`, `what_didnt_work`, `blast_radius_outcome`. The entry traces to the task's pre-existing entry (created at task creation by `specflow:task` Phase D, if any) by id; if no prior entry exists, the skill creates one. Verifies: Goal Outcome surface (h).' No new R-level requirement added — the goal field's mention plus the Phase 3 architectural scope item are sufficient.

da-r1-f1.rationale: Cross-artefact ambiguity is real. The plugin's binary present/absent framing missed the present-but-failing third path. Phase 1's `specflow:design` Codex degraded-path is the precedent for the loud-fallback shape. Extending R8 + AC-6 closes the gap.
da-r1-f1.revision_applied: R8 extended with present-but-failing clause: 'When the agent-teams plugin is detected but `team-spawn` returns an error (preset name unmatched, plugin version-skew, plugin internal error), `specflow:develop` falls back to sequential single-specialist invocation per R9's stack-match logic AND surfaces the failure to the user as a chat-line warning (e.g. `[agent-teams: team-spawn failed for preset {name} — falling back to single-specialist {agent}]`). The fallback does NOT abort the task; the user can intervene if needed.' AC-6 extended with sub-clause: 'When `team-spawn` returns an error, the plan logs `team-spawn failed: {error}; fell back to single-specialist invoked: agent={agent-name}`.'
